ChaosPilot — Project Evaluation & Incident Resilience Report

System: ChaosPilot Autonomous AI Chaos Engineering & Incident Postmortem Engine

Date of Report: November 20, 2026 | Status: Verified & Production-Benchmarked

Contributors: Project Lead & Presenter (Architecture & UI/UX), Aman (Simulator & Ingestion), Anurag (ML Anomaly Detector), Dhruv (Dashboard & 3D Core)

1. Executive Summary

ChaosPilot is an AI-powered chaos engineering lab on a microservices stack (gateway, auth, orders, payments, cache, db). The system deterministically simulates real-world failure dynamics, monitors 10-dimensional temporal telemetry streams, detects non-linear anomalies via an unsupervised Isolation Forest model, and synthesizes grounded postmortem reports with an LLM agent without hallucinated root causes.

2. Machine Learning Anomaly Detection Model Metrics

The detector isolates anomalous microservice behavior across sliding temporal windows using an Isolation Forest trained on healthy baseline telemetry.

Hyperparameter / Metric Recorded Value Context / Benchmark Purpose
Model Algorithm IsolationForest (scikit-learn 1.9.0) Unsupervised outlier tree isolation
Contamination Factor 0.02 (2.0%) Expected proportion of anomalous windows in baseline traffic
Estimators (Trees) 200 trees Ensemble stability & false-positive minimization
Optimal F1 Threshold 0.6857 (sweep calibrated) Maximizes precision/recall harmonic mean
Validation Precision 97.96% (0.9796) Only 2 false positives out of 1,606 normal windows
Validation Recall 92.31% (0.9231) 96 true anomalies flagged out of 104 fault windows
Validation F1 Score 95.05% (0.9505) Top-tier anomaly classification performance
Validation Overall Accuracy 99.42% (0.9942) Evaluated across 1,710 contiguous validation windows
Hold-out Test Precision 94.12% (0.9412) Unseen hold-out split (1,866 windows evaluated)
Kill Fault Detection Recall 100.0% (56/56) Zero missed service outages

3. Confusion Matrix Analysis

Evaluation of 1,368 time windows under calibrated decision threshold 0.57 yields an overall diagnostic accuracy of 99.19% with an exceptionally low 0.3% false-positive rate.

Figure 1: Confusion Matrix of Isolation Forest Anomaly Detector (F1 = 0.97, Threshold = 0.57)
  • True Negatives (Normal classified as Normal): 1,184 windows (86.5%)
  • False Positives (Normal misclassified as Fault): 4 windows (0.3%)
  • False Negatives (Fault missed by detector): 7 windows (0.5%)
  • True Positives (Fault successfully isolated): 173 windows (12.6%)

4. Resilience Benchmark & Compare Panel Results

Microservice resilience is quantified on a strict 0–100 scale penalizing service crashes (-15 pts) and latency degradation (-6 pts), granting a +10 containment bonus when circuit-breakers protect unaffected downstream nodes:

Score = max(0, min(100, 100 - (15 × N_failed) - (6 × N_degraded) + Bonus))
Run ID Fault Type Target Fixes OFF Fixes ON Delta Blast Radius & Containment Result
Run 1 latency (+2000ms) gateway 94.0 100.0 +6.0 Gateway p50 surged from 56.3ms to 2059.8ms. In resilient mode, timeouts prevented queue stalls (+10 bonus).
Run 2 memory (256MB leak) cache 82.0 89.0 +7.0 Cache memory saturation degraded auth lookups; resilient fallback kept checkout operational.
Run 3 kill (process crash) gateway 70.0 100.0 +30.0 100% checkout failure without fixes; self-healing container recovery fully restored service.

5. Agent Incident Postmortem Generation

Raw Collector Summary (Run #1):

Experiment #1: latency on gateway from scenario #1 "github activity: PushEvent" (source: github, data: live, fixes=off). Baseline: gateway p50 56.3ms, errors 0/23. Fault: gateway p50 2059.8ms, errors 0/4. Gateway latency moved +2004ms during the fault (36.6x baseline). Resilience score: 94/100.

Structured LLM Incident Postmortem (Automated Agent Synthesis):

Root Cause: Injected 2000ms artificial latency on service gateway caused checkout request times to spike from 56.3ms baseline to 2059.8ms (36.6x increase) with resilience safeguards disabled.

Blast Radius: Primary entrypoint gateway degraded; synthetic user checkout path stalled; downstream dependencies auth and orders experienced secondary connection starvation.

Remediation Actions:

  1. Add client-side timeout of 1000ms with circuit breaker tripping after 3 consecutive failures.
  2. Implement async queue offloading for non-critical telemetry and audit logging.
  3. Configure dynamic autoscaling alerts triggered when p95 latency exceeds 3x learned baseline.
